reviews.text:
Today I went to this veterinary practice with a cat I found on the street, and Dr. Carbonelli saw us without even making an appointment. He examined the cat
(free of charge) and recommended all the necessary tests. Recommended!
Thanks again

My two dachshunds have been treated and cared for by the practice's doctors on several occasions with great professionalism and attention, always making themselves available to our needs. I highly recommend them for their great medical and human professionalism.
Dr. Piergiorgio and his staff are the BEST, He is so warm and kind and very thorough with my dog Chaplin, a 100 lb. English Cream Golden Retriever now 10 years old.

Fantastic... I've taken all my pets, 3 dogs and 6 cats, for neutering/spaying and various checkups over the years.
Always available and, above all, professional; a true reference!
Among the most significant surgeries my four-legged friends have had to undergo, I'd like to mention two in particular:
Years ago, I found an elderly cat abandoned on the street and, without thinking twice, I brought him home and then to them for a general checkup. I immediately noticed excessive discharge coming from one eye; to my inexperienced eye, it looked like he might lose his sight. They operated on him, after blood tests given his age, and now that eye is perfect. In September, if his age allows, we'll operate on the other one as well.
The second episode occurred a few weeks ago: an operation under total sedation for one of my dogs. He hadn't eaten for a few days, he's always had problems with his teeth, and in the past, Dr. Piergiorgio had already pulled a few teeth that needed to be removed. I called in the afternoon, and the next day he was available to remove more teeth and a small cyst under his chin. Within a day, my dog ​​was eating solids again, and the wound under his chin is now gone.
What can I say? I trust them implicitly.

My Pacchia had a laparoscopic spay/neuter operation with Dr. Carbonelli. It was as if nothing had happened; the next day she was happily climbing up. The price? Half of what was advertised online. P.S. My (former) vet doesn't do laparoscopy and is wrong (down with Elizabethan collars, even for cats!!)
Always very professional and helpful. They were there whenever I needed help for my dog.
A reliable and competent veterinary practice. Dr. Carbonelli and Dr. Lucia were always very attentive and affectionate with our cat. Highly recommended!

I booked an appointment based on the positive reviews. I should point out that my veterinarian has been with us for a long time, and this was a second opinion regarding some purely dermatological concerns.
I found the visit rushed and lacking empathy. The doctor was unable to answer some of my specific questions—the reason for the dermatological visit—and ultimately failed to provide a definitive diagnosis, prescribing a nonspecific treatment.
She also took a sample, but to date, months later, the results have never arrived. When I called for a response, I was told that perhaps the sample was lost because they couldn't find anything.
Once again, I was speechless.
So, with a heavy heart, I have to say that it was a disappointing experience for us, and I don't feel comfortable recommending her, especially since I have nothing to compare it to.
Serious, professional and always available veterinarian, also open during the month of August!!!
Fantastic vet, very knowledgeable and friendly, 360 degrees
always kind, attentive and professional, I find myself very well, highly recommended, thank you very much!!

A little over a year ago, I reluctantly took my cat to be spayed.

Laparoscopic spay (€250) went badly.

At the end of the procedure, the cat had two stitches, one of which, within reach of her snout, obviously became infected. But according to them, a collar wouldn't have been necessary.

I called repeatedly for check-ups soon afterward, because the lowest point was still a little swollen.
They thought it was normal. And they reassured me and sent me home.
One Friday morning, a few days after the last visit, while I was at home, I noticed that it was still swollen and sent videos and photos to the doctor, who didn't respond because she was obviously busy. I saw the cat trying to lick the wound, stopped her immediately, and noticed pus coming out. I called immediately, but the doctor wasn't there. I rushed to them anyway, urgently, in the early afternoon.

Result:
Antibiotics and Elizabethan collar
Diarrhea and lactic acid bacteria
Days of home-made dressings, done by me. The wound was still oozing serum.

It could have ended like this instead...

A few days later, we returned to finally remove the stitches. The wound hadn't healed completely.
A piece of blue thread remained inside. I removed it at home while I was dressing her.
The hole slowly healed.

They had the nerve to say that my cat had been a bit unlucky.

We were certainly extremely unlucky to meet you.

A terrible experience, unfortunately, but I hope this feedback can help her improve.

This veterinary practice was a real discovery for us. We've had a kitten here for a few months, and we immediately trusted Dr. Carbonelli. He welcomed us with professionalism, attention, and a touch of kindness, essential for a new journey with a puppy.
He's always been available and reliable, even for quick checkups, in a welcoming environment that's a point of reference for all the four-legged patients in the neighborhood.
